reviewer.agent: Claude Code (file handoff; environment names the handoff channel)

themes.label: National AI scientific leadership
themes.definition: Speaker cites own country's scientists as leaders in AI as a national strength.
themes.inclusion: Passages boasting national AI research or talent leadership.
themes.boundary_cases: If AI appears only in a list of national strengths without claims of leadership, use AI_TECH_LIST_MENTION.

examples.quote: Our scientists are leaders in artificial intelligence and clean technology.

themes.label: AI as a citizen worry
themes.definition: AI mentioned as something ordinary citizens are worried about, alongside cost of living, foreign interference and disinformation, without elaboration.
themes.inclusion: Passages reporting public anxiety or concern about AI.
themes.exclusion: Passages that specify what the AI risk is (use the specific risk code).
themes.boundary_cases: When disinformation is listed next to AI but not linked causally, keep this code rather than AI_DISINFORMATION.

examples.quote: They are also concerned about artificial intelligence, foreign interference, misinformation and disinformation.

themes.label: Championing responsible AI development
themes.definition: Brief commitment to be a trusted voice defending responsible AI development internationally, without specifying mechanisms.
themes.inclusion: Passages pledging to promote responsible development of AI as a foreign policy priority.
themes.exclusion: Concrete rules or institutional proposals (use AI_GLOBAL_GOVERNANCE).
themes.boundary_cases: If a specific international framework is named, use AI_GLOBAL_GOVERNANCE instead.

examples.quote: Canada will remain a voice that can be trusted, to defend maritime security, international law, and the responsible development of artificial intelligence

value.rationale: All three Canadian passages mention AI only briefly: as a national scientific strength, as a public worry listed with disinformation, and as a foreign-policy commitment to responsible development.
